style: busy mom, plain full sentences; once writes the younger brother's name (Dev) when she means Priya

situations.name: Talking to family on the phone (grandma, aunt)
situations.feared_outcome: There will be a long silence and they'll think I'm weird

behaviors.text: Won't come to the phone when grandma or her aunt calls; says she's busy or goes to her room
Writes what she will say on a sticky note and reads it word for word

accommodations.text: Mom tells the relative Priya is busy or in the shower

situations.name: Calling a business on the phone (pizza place, library, dentist)
situations.feared_outcome: They'll ask me something I don't know and I'll freeze

behaviors.text: Dials, then hands the phone back to mom before it rings
Hung up as soon as the library worker answered

accommodations.text: Dad does it online instead (orders food, renews library books) so nobody has to call

behaviors.text: Stays at the back of the line in drills so the coach won't pick her to demonstrate
Keeps looking over to check that mom is still on the sideline

accommodations.text: Mom asked the coach not to make her demonstrate in front of the team

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Priya said she was doing homework and wouldn't come to the phone.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I told Grandma she was busy and would call back.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Stayed at the very back of every line during drills. Looked over at me a lot.
I asked her to call it in. She dialed and then handed the phone back to me before it even rang.
Dev wouldn't get on the phone to say happy birthday. Went to her room and shut the door.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Told Rina she was in the shower.
monitoring_log.trap: parent wrote the 6-year-old brother's name (Dev) but means Priya; 'her room' and the situation show it is Priya

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Played okay but kept checking where I was standing. When the coach asked for a volunteer to show the throw-in she moved behind two other girls.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Cheered for her. We talked about it a little in the car.

monitoring_log.parent_words: She tried calling the library to renew her books because I said I wasn't going to do it for her. The lady picked up and Priya just hung up. Then she cried a little and her dad renewed them online. She said it was an 8 after.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: She came to the phone! She had written what she wanted to say on a sticky note and read it off word for word. Got through about two minutes.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Told her afterward I was proud of her.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Back of the line again for every drill.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Before practice I asked Coach Dana not to make her demonstrate anything in front of the team.

voice_notes.text: so um priya was supposed to call the dentist to ask what time her appointment is that was the deal we made and she got as far as dialing and then she gave me the phone back before it rang um she said it was like an eight

ok two things from today um at practice she was at the back again for the passing drill and kept looking over at me like every minute and then tonight grandma called and she actually talked but she had her little sticky note and she read the whole thing off it

turns.text: Okay, we're recording. Priya, Mom, good to see you both. Let's start where we always start. How did the week go? Mom, I read through your log, thank you for being so thorough.
It was a phone week. Almost everything I wrote down was about the phone. And soccer.

Let's take the phone first. I noticed there were two kinds of calls on there. Some were calls with family, like Grandma and your aunt. And some were calls to places, like the pizza place and the library. Priya, are those the same for you, or different?
Different.
How are they different?
With Grandma, she always asks about school, and then I say fine, and then nobody says anything. And it's quiet. And she probably thinks I'm weird because I don't have anything to say.
So with Grandma, the scary part is the silence. What about calling the pizza place?
That's worse. Because they could ask me anything. Like, do you want a large, or what's your address, or is that pickup. And I won't know, and I'll just freeze, and they'll be waiting.

That's really helpful, Priya. Those are two different worries. With family it's the silence, and them thinking you're weird. With a business it's being asked something you don't know and freezing. So we're going to keep those as two separate things on your list.
I hadn't thought about it like that. I just thought, phone.
It's easy to lump them together. Let's get numbers on both. Priya, zero to ten, how scary is calling Grandma right now?
Like a seven. Maybe a six now.
Why maybe a six now?
Because I did it on Monday. With my note.
She did. She came to the phone and talked for about two minutes. She had written it all out on a sticky note first.
That's a real step. You came to the phone when the phone was scary. Can I ask about the note? What was on it?
Like, hi Grandma, school is good, I have a soccer game Saturday, how is your garden. And then bye, love you.
So the whole conversation was on there.
Yeah. So there wouldn't be a quiet part.

That makes sense. The note is doing a job for you. It's making sure the silence never happens. The tricky thing is, if the silence never happens, you never get to find out what happens when it does. Whether Grandma actually thinks you're weird, or whether she just says something else.
She'd probably just talk about her tomatoes.
She would absolutely talk about her tomatoes.
That's a pretty good guess. Okay, and calling a place, like the pizza place or the library. Zero to ten?
Eight.
Eight. Mom, tell me about the library.

So I told her I wasn't going to renew her books for her, she had to call. And she did call, she dialed and everything. The woman picked up, said the library name, and Priya just hung up. Then she was upset, and honestly my husband just went online and renewed them because they were due that day.
Okay. So she got further than the pizza place, where the phone went back to you before it rang. This time she was on the call and hung up when someone answered. And then the books got renewed online.
Right. He does that a lot. He orders the food online too. He says it's just easier and why make her suffer.

I hear that, and he's not wrong that it's easier this week. We'll talk about that piece. I want to hold calling places for a bit, though. An eight is a big jump from where we are. Let's do soccer and then come back to a plan.
Soccer is fine, really. She likes soccer. She's just always at the back.
Priya, what's at the back?
If you're at the back, Coach Dana picks someone at the front to show the drill. So it's not me.
And when you look over at Mom during practice?
I just want to see if she's still there.
How scary is practice, zero to ten?
Five. Games are less, actually. Like a four.
I should say, I did ask the coach this week not to make her demonstrate. I thought I was helping.

That came from a kind place. It's worth noticing that it works the same way the sticky note does, and the back of the line does. It makes sure the scary part doesn't happen. We don't have to undo it today. Let's just put it on the list so we can look at it later.
Okay. Fair.
Priya, can I ask you one more thing about soccer? When you look over and Mom is there, what does that do for you?
I don't know. It's just good. Like, if something happens.
What kind of something?
Like if I mess up a drill in front of everybody. Or if Coach yells. She doesn't really yell. But if she did.

So Mom on the sideline is a bit like the sticky note. Something that helps you feel ready in case it goes wrong. That's really useful for me to know. We're not going to change soccer this week, either. I just want us to see the pattern. Mom, does that match what you see from the sideline?
It does. She looks over constantly. I had honestly thought it was sweet. Like she wanted me to watch her play. Some of it probably is that.
It can be both. Kids do like to be watched. The way to tell the difference is what happens if you're not there. Has that ever happened?
Once, in the spring. I had to take Dev to a doctor's appointment and his dad took her instead. She was fine, I think. She said she was fine.
I was fine. It was boring without you, though.
That's good to know. Okay. Let's put a plan together, because there's a lot here and I don't want to do all of it at once.
So here's my suggestion for this week, and Priya, you get a vote. Grandma calls a lot, right?
Like every two days.

Great, that's lots of practice. This week, when Grandma calls, you come to the phone. Every time, at least for one minute. And instead of the whole conversation on the sticky note, you're allowed three words on it. Just three. Like school, soccer, garden.
Three words? What if I run out?
Then there might be a quiet bit. And you get to see what Grandma does in the quiet bit. My guess is tomatoes.
Okay. Three words.
And I shouldn't tell her Priya's busy anymore.
Right. When Grandma calls and asks for Priya, you hand her the phone. No more she's in the shower. Can you do that?
Yes. And the online thing, with my husband?
Leave it for this week. We're not doing calls to places yet. We'll build up to those. Just keep writing them down if they come up, with the number.
So I don't have to call the pizza place.
Not this week. This week is Grandma, and the three-word note. Mom, keep logging each call and the number Priya gives you. I'll see you both next Thursday.

topics: Two different phone situations: family calls (fear of silence and seeming weird) and calls to businesses (fear of being asked something and freezing)

Soccer: stays at the back so the coach won't pick her, checks mom is on the sideline; mom asked coach not to make her demonstrate
agreed: Priya comes to the phone every time Grandma calls, for at least one minute
Sticky note limited to three words instead of a full script
Mom hands her the phone and stops saying she is busy
Calls to businesses are on hold this week; just log them if they come up
Mom logs each call and Priya's number

must_not_appear: Priya will call a business (pizza place, library) this week
Dad will stop ordering or renewing online this week
